content.text: {"relation":"MATCH","consensus_summary":"All four blind responses identify the primary symbolic meaning of 'harvest' as the eschatological ingathering at the end of the age — God gathering the righteous (wheat) and judging/destroying the wicked (weeds/chaff burned) — anchored chiefly in Matthew 13:24-43, Revelation 14:14-20, Joel 3:13, and Matthew 3:12/Luke 3:17. Widely acknowledged secondary senses include the evangelistic 'harvest of souls,' sowing-and-reaping moral recompense, firstfruits/resurrection typology, and harvest as covenant blessing.","book_summary":"The book defines harvest as 'the end of the age, when the field of mankind is reaped — the wheat gathered, the chaff burned,' citing Joel 3:13 and Matthew 13:39.","consensus_core_identification":"Harvest = the end-of-the-age eschatological reaping of humanity: gathering of the righteous and judgment/destruction of the wicked.","book_core_identification":"Harvest = the end of the age, when mankind is reaped: wheat gathered, chaff burned.","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"SAME_CASES","boundary_disagreement":"None of substance. The book's glossary entry does not enumerate the consensus's secondary uses (evangelistic harvest, sowing/reaping recompense, firstfruits typology), but it does not deny them; its stated core is identical to the consensus primary meaning. The dual aspect (gathering the saved / burning the wicked) is preserved verbatim.","material_contradiction":"None. Both identify the same referent — the end-of-the-age reaping with its salvation/judgment duality.","rationale":"The book's definition is essentially a paraphrase of the consensus primary meaning: 'the harvest is the end of the age' (Matt 13:39) with the wheat/chaff duality that all four responses foreground. Matthew 13:39 is cited by every consensus response, and Joel 3:13 by three of four. The absence of secondary senses in a terse glossary entry is immaterial detail, not a boundary restriction, since the entry does not claim exclusivity against the evangelistic or moral-reaping uses. Core identifications are equivalent; this is a MATCH.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"One could argue the book implicitly narrows the symbol by omitting the very widespread evangelistic 'harvest of souls' sense (which Responses A and B call 'dominant' in popular usage), so the entry could be read as REFINED (BOOK_SUBSET). However, a short glossary stating the primary meaning without listing alternatives is not a material boundary claim, and the consensus itself ranks the eschatological sense as primary.","confidence":"high"}
